summary: Hakuun Yasutani (1885–1973) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He graduated from Tokyo Prefectural Toshima Normal School and studied under teachers including Daiun Sogaku Harada, Bokusan Nishiari, and Genpo Tsuyama. He founded the Sanbo Kyodan in 1954.

Hakuyu Hadano (1916–1989) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He spent his career at Tohoku University, serving as Assistant Professor (attested 1953–1959) and later becoming Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and San Francisco State University under teachers including Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Yasutani. A priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission (1956), he founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles.

Halle O'Neal specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas (attested 2011) under Sherry Fowler. As of 2026, she is Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990), an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Mahabodhi College, SOAS, the University of Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara (ca. 1957–1990).
Hang Kan (born 1965) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Bai Su. He served as the Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has been a faculty member at Haverford College (attested 2009 and 2019).

Hanna Havnevik works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at the University of Oslo, serving as Professor (attested 2006–2008) and later Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Hanns Oertel (1868–1952) specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing his doctorate at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale (1891–1917), the University of Marburg (1922), and held a chair at the University of Munich (1925–1935).

Hanns-Peter Schmidt (1930–2017) was an Indology and Iranian scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf. He held posts at Tübingen and Deccan College before serving as Professor at UCLA (1965–2000).

Hans Delbrück (1848–1929) was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (ca. 1869–1873). He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (ca. 1881–1921) and Frederick William University Berlin (1885).

Hans Harder (born 1966) is an Indologist who studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg, completing his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das. He served as Assistent at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and joined the Heidelberg University editorial board in 2007.

Hans Hartog (born 1912) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Wuppertal/Bethel, and Munich before earning his PhD at the University of Marburg (1937–1939) under doctoral supervisor Friedrich Heiler.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder (1896–1957) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (ca. 1930–1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (ca. 1931–1946), and the University of Göttingen (ca. 1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock (born 1938) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed graduate degrees at Northwestern University and Yale University and served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (ca. 1967–2007).
Hans Krahe (1898–1965) was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Würzburg (ca. 1936–1946), Heidelberg University (ca. 1947–1949), and the University of Tübingen (ca. 1949–1965).

Hans Küng (1928–2021) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, and the Catholic University of Paris, and held a post at the University of Tübingen (ca. 1960–1996).
Hans Martin Krämer (born 1972) works in Japanology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Ruhr University Bochum from ca. 2000 to 2005 and held a post there around 2008.

Hans T. Bakker (born 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink. He held a post at the University of Groningen (ca. 1996–2013) and served as a curator at the British Museum (2014).

Hans Urs von Balthasar (1905–1988) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Zurich from ca. 1924 to 1928 and studied under Bernhard Geiger between 1924 and 1926.
